e.text: Digital-first A1 hit 23.7%, triple the 8.1% benchmark; asking the Critic how to push it further.

e.note: Reading results for A1, A2

critique.summary: A1 is the clear leader: 23.7% reach (10th percentile 22.3%) at $804 per point, nearly 3x the benchmark's 8.1% and well ahead of A2's 17.4%, driven by city-wide targeted ads plus podcasts and the Nike Training Club drop. Hyper-local seeding is not paying off: A2's street teams and zone partners each earn under 1% of adoption, and the hot zones together hold only about 7% of the natural audience.

findings.finding: Reaches 23.7% (22.3%–24.9%) at $804 per point versus the benchmark's $1887, with 55.4% of adoption from word of mouth and even reach across districts (21.8%–25.1%).
The podcasts are costly per credit: Monday Morning Podcast earns 5.5% for $3500 and The Champs earns 4.5% for $3450, while the $2000 Nike Training Club drop earns 5.9%.
The Nike collab starts on day 20 and The Champs podcast runs on day 25, which leaves less time for word of mouth to compound before launch.
Reaches 17.4% (16.5%–18.3%) at $1056 per point; the five street teams on days 6–14 earn only 0.1%–0.2% each for $450 apiece, and zone partners earn 0.5%–0.6% for $300.
The Big Plate Cafe pop-up on day 48 earns 0.8% for $2500, too late and too local, while the Brentford co-drop earns 4.7% for $2000, close to Nike's return.
Reaches 8.1% at $1887 per point; untargeted broad ads earn 28.1% of adoption, and its street teams earn 0%.

changes.change: Start from A1, and move collab:43A36E73 (Nike Training Club) from day 20 to day 0–5 so it runs for about 51 days.
changes.why: Nike has A1's best cost per credit, and an earlier start gives word of mouth more time to compound.

changes.change: Add collab:4FCDD007 (Brentford F.C., $2000) starting day 5, funded by dropping podcast:BF2C0255 (The Champs, $3450).
changes.why: Brentford earned 4.7% for $2000 in A2, while The Champs earned 4.5% for $3450.

changes.change: Move podcast:853C9C96 (Monday Morning Podcast) from day 10 to around day 3.
changes.why: Earlier exposure lengthens the word-of-mouth runway.

changes.change: Do not add any street teams, zone partners or the day-48 popup:97F3C556.
changes.why: Each earned 0.1%–0.8% of adoption in A2, and the five hot zones hold only about 7% of the natural audience.

Hyper-local seeding is not paying off: A2's street teams and zone partners each earn under 1% of adoption, and the hot zones together hold only about 7% of the natural audience.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B1

plan.headline: Nike drop plus targeted ads and two podcasts: 26% simulated natural-audience reach, 3.2× benchmark
plan.summary: The bet is digital-first: city-wide interest-targeted social ads and a co-branded Nike Training Club drop running from day 0, boosted by two Cole Palmer-driven podcast reads early in the run. Qloo taste data shows London's under-24 audience over-indexes on Nike (0.92), the Monday Morning Podcast (0.92) and The Champs (0.90), pulled in by Cole Palmer and Chelsea F.C. In a simulation built on that taste data, not a guarantee, the plan reaches about 26% of the natural audience (range 25–27%), roughly 3.2× the 8.1% benchmark, at $731 per point of reach versus $1,887, with word of mouth driving 57% of adoption.
